title: GS-Fuse: Granger-Supervised Gated Fusion and Multi-Granularity Alignment for Event-Driven Financial Forecasting

problem.claim: Forecasting the market impact of salient financial events is important for investors and policymakers.

gap.claim: Existing multimodal time-series models typically fuse text and prices symmetrically and lack an explicit mechanism for determining when event text is predictive.

contributions.claim: GS-Fuse uses a Granger-supervised, causal-aware gated fusion module to incorporate event text when it provides incremental predictive value beyond historical prices.
GS-Fuse jointly aligns high-level event representations and fine-grained textual cues with future market trajectories through multi-granularity alignment.
GS-Fuse is designed as a plug-and-play adapter for off-the-shelf large language models and time-series foundation models across market settings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GS-Fuse consistently outperforms state-of-the-art time-series and multimodal baselines on real-world financial datasets across multiple assets and forecasting horizons.

narrative_sequence.summary: Event-impact forecasting is presented as important for financial decision-makers.
Existing multimodal models are described as inadequate for directional event-to-price relationships and heterogeneous signal roles.
GS-Fuse introduces gated fusion supervised by Granger-style incremental predictiveness and multi-granularity alignment.
The framework is described as adaptable across model backbones and market settings.
The authors report consistent superiority over stated baseline classes across assets and forecasting horizons.

source_observation.claim: The framework gates event-text use based on incremental predictive value beyond historical prices.

interpretation.claim: Multimodal systems may benefit from conditional modality use instead of always-weighted fusion.

application.claim: Use predictive-value-aware gating when one modality may be informative only for some inputs or periods.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this gating strategy is beneficial outside the reported financial forecasting settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, assets, forecasting horizons, metrics, or baseline implementations.
The abstract does not provide quantitative performance values or independent verification.
The abstract does not describe ablations, statistical significance, or reproducibility details.
